title: Injectivity and flat cokernels at the limit of localized module-arrow diagrams
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and let $R_i	o S_i$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with transition ring maps $r_{ji},s_{ji}$ for $i\le j$, respecting identity and composition and commuting with $R_i	o S_i$. Let $R	o S$ be their ring colimit with compatible ring cocones $r_i:R_i	o R$, $s_i:S_i	o S$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $M_i,N_i$ be $S_i$-modules, $u_i:M_i	o N_i$ be $S_i$-linear, and let their additive transitions $m_{ji},n_{ji}$ be semilinear over $s_{ji}$, respect identities and composition, and satisfy $n_{ji}u_i=u_jm_{ji}$. Let $M,N$ be $S$-modules, with compatible additive cocones $\mu_i,
u_i$ semilinear over $s_i$, and let $u:M	o N$ be $S$-linear with $
u_i u_i=u\mu_i$. Suppose these cocones exhibit $M,N$ as algebraic colimits of the underlying abelian groups: every element comes from a stage and equality of two representatives is detected at a common later stage. Suppose for every $i$ the canonical maps $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S	o M$ and $N_i\otimes_{S_i}S	o N$, $x\otimes s\mapsto s\mu_i(x)$ and $y\otimes s\mapsto s
u_i(y)$, are isomorphisms carrying $u_i\otimes1$ to $u$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Suppose also that $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R	o S$, $a\otimes r\mapsto s_i(a)\varphi(r)$, where $\varphi:R	o S$ is the colimit ring map, is a localization at a multiplicative subset for every $i$ (denominators become units, every target element is a fraction, and every source element mapping to zero is killed by a denominator). Put $C_i=N_i/u_i(M_i)$ and $C=N/u(M)$. Assume that for some $i_0$, every $u_j$ with $j\ge i_0$ is injective and every $C_j$ with $j\ge i_0$ is flat over $R_j$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $u$ is injective and $C$ is flat over $R$. For every $i$ the canonical map $C_i\otimes_{S_i}S	o C$, $[y]\otimes s\mapsto s[
u_i(y)]$, is an isomorphism. No locality, Noetherianity, or finite generation is assumed. All sets and objects may be placed in one common sufficiently large universe.

proof.text: Let $x\in\ker u$. Choose $i$ and $x_i\in M_i$ with $x=\mu_i(x_i)$. Then $\nu_i(u_i(x_i))=0$. The assumed detection of equality in the additive colimit $N$, applied to $u_i(x_i)$ and $0\in N_i$, gives $j\ge i$ with $n_{ji}(u_i(x_i))=0$. Choose $k\ge j,i_0$. Commutation with the arrows gives $u_k(m_{ki}(x_i))=n_{kj}n_{ji}(u_i(x_i))=0$. Since $u_k$ is injective, $m_{ki}(x_i)=0$, so $x=\mu_k(m_{ki}(x_i))=0$. Applying this to a difference proves injectivity of $u$.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), final sentence; Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit), here used directly as a hypothesis of the item

proof.text: Fix any $i$, not necessarily on the eventual tail. Write $p_i:N_i\to C_i$ and $p:N\to C$ for quotient maps. The sequence $M_i\xrightarrow{u_i}N_i\xrightarrow{p_i}C_i\to0$ is right exact by the definition of $C_i$. Tensor right exactness gives a surjection $q_i=p_i\otimes1:N_i\otimes_{S_i}S\to C_i\otimes_{S_i}S$ with kernel $\operatorname{im}(u_i\otimes1)$. The assumed scalar-extension isomorphisms identify this image with $u(M)$ inside $N$. Thus $p$ induces an isomorphism $h_i:C_i\otimes_{S_i}S\to C$: its inverse sends $[n]$ to $q_i(\beta_i^{-1}(n))$, where $\beta_i:N_i\otimes_{S_i}S\simeq N$ is the given isomorphism. This is well defined because changing $n$ by $u(m)$ changes $\beta_i^{-1}(n)$ by an element of $\operatorname{im}(u_i\otimes1)$. The two composites are identities after precomposing with the surjective quotient maps. The formula is $h_i([y]\otimes s)=s[\nu_i(y)]$, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact); cokernel identification in the final passage of Tag 046Y

proof.text: Use the existing localized-base-change quotient-flatness lemma with its rings $(R,S,R\prime,S\prime)=(R_{i_0},S_{i_0},R,S)$, module $C_{i_0}$, and ideal $I=(0)$. The scalar towers commute by the ring cocones, and its localization map is exactly the map $S_{i_0}\otimes_{R_{i_0}}R\to S$ assumed here. Its input $(R_{i_0}/0)\otimes_{R_{i_0}}C_{i_0}\simeq C_{i_0}$ is flat by the tail hypothesis. Since $0R=0$, its conclusion says $S\otimes_{S_{i_0}}C_{i_0}$ is flat over $R$. The identifications $R/0\simeq R$ and $(R/0)\otimes_RP\simeq P$ send $[r]\otimes p$ to $rp$, with inverse $p\mapsto[1]\otimes p$. Tensor symmetry $s\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes s$ (inverse $c\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes c$), followed by $h_{i_0}$ from step 2, identifies this module $R$-linearly with $C$. Flatness is invariant under this isomorphism: for an injective map of $R$-modules, the two tensor maps are conjugate via the isomorphism and its inverse. Hence $C$ is $R$-flat.
